newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian rail union calls safety go-slow.
newsitem.headline: Italian rail union calls safety go-slow.

text.p: A trades union representing Italian train drivers said on Friday that it had called a go-slow from next week to press for a safety review following the derailment of a high-speed train in which eight people were killed.
COMU, one of several unions in the industry, said it had ordered members to keep to speed below the limits set out for various sections of track and not to exceed 150 kph (95 mph).

A statement said the action would begin at 1230 GMT next Monday and continue until the state railway company, Ferrovie dello Stato (FS), had meet the union's demands for a joint review of safety systems, track maintenance and working hours.

COMU and other unions held a two-hour strike on Thursday over safety following last Sunday's accident, which occurred near the northern city of Piacenza when the Milan-Rome high-speed "Pendolino" train derailed.

FS managing director Giancarlo Cimoli said earlier this week that there was no immediate evidence that the train, built to tilt into bends at speed, had been faulty or that the track on which it was travelling had been defective.
He added, however, that rail safety would be looked at closely.
Authorities have focused on speed as a possible cause for the derailment of the train, Italy's fastest.
